rules.sentence: Venous anomalies may be associated with cavernous malformations (see below), which do carry some bleeding risk.
If bleeding does occur, it rarely produces mass effect or significant symptoms.
Bleeding is usually of small volume, causing slight mass effect only.
The bleeding risk for single cavernous malformations is 0.7–1.5% per year and may be higher for patients with prior clinical hemorrhage or multiple malformations.
Seizures may occur if the malformation is located near the cerebral cortex.
Surgical resection eliminates bleeding risk and may reduce seizure risk, but it is usually reserved for those malformations that form near the brain surface.
Radiation treatment has not been shown to be of benefit.
